entries.title: Reading time is recorded for every reader
entries.body: The strip showing where you are in an article shades the parts you have spent time on. This used to need the Experimental features switch; it is on for everyone, on their own articles, so a stretch you read no longer looks unread later. There is no control to switch it off or erase what it has recorded. Quiz's 'Only what I've read' filter comes with it, and a quiz you return to opens at the first question you have not answered.

entries.title: Check a Debate claim in Chat
entries.body: With the Experimental features switch on, each claim in Debate on your own articles has a button that starts a conversation about it, and a mark under the claim reopens that conversation later. Chat's list also shows conversations started in Remember, and marks each row with where it began: Debate, Remember, or a passage. A Remember conversation opens back in Remember. On a phone, the list shows more of each conversation's opening question.

entries.title: Citations shows how often a work is cited
entries.body: With the Experimental features switch on, Citations shows how many times a cited work has itself been cited, and the date that figure was read. The count is Crossref's, and appears only for works the app has matched there. Chat can draw on these counts. A DOI link containing encoded characters is no longer encoded a second time.

entries.title: Brief summaries run a little longer
entries.body: Brief aims for about 100 words rather than 80. Fuller is asked to explain a name the piece introduces at its first use, and to introduce a thing before referring to it; existing summaries are marked out of date, not rewritten. Adding your first profile also marks what was written before it, and most modes offer a rewrite.

entries.title: Quick search from the command bar
entries.body: Ask the command bar to find something and it offers Quick search first, ahead of exact-words Find. Press the microphone's Stop twice quickly there and it acts on what you said. Search's box has a clear button. The thorough search's description is corrected to 'usually about ten seconds'; the search itself is no faster.

entries.title: The AI tidies the titles of new articles
entries.body: When you add an article, its title in your library is tidied by the AI, which is given only the title, the site's name and the language, and may make only light edits. Titles you already have are unchanged. The privacy page now says the AI is used for this. A shared article's link preview uses a picture from the article when one is suitable.

entries.title: Answers stay put while they are written
entries.body: In Chat, Remember and chats about a passage, the panel used to scroll down with each arriving line of a typed answer, so the first sentence left the screen while you were still reading it. The start of the answer now holds its place, and Latest takes you to the end.

entries.title: Dropped AI requests are tried again
entries.body: A request to the AI service that is dropped or briefly refused is tried again, up to three attempts in most cases, instead of failing at once. When the fuller outline of a long document could not be made, Structure says so, and its owner can press Try again. An article with a damaged outline opens instead of failing.
